sections.content:
26,515 people

were counted on the census as "therapy professionals (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may plan and apply physical and therapeutic treatments and activities to assist recovery from physical and mental illness and to minimise the effects of disabilities not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "therapy professionals (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "therapy professionals (other)", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "therapy professionals (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "therapy professionals (other)" included:

  • electronics engineers
  • senior care workers
  • business associate professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "therapy professionals (other)" there were more women than men (71.4% compared with 28.6%).

This means "therapy professionals (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 28.6% and women made up 71.4% of "therapy professionals (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "therapy professionals (other)" included:

  • local government administrative occupations
  • officers of non-governmental organisations
  • financial administrative occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "therapy professionals (other)", 9.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (51.8% compared with 48.2%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (56.9%) than an employee (43.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Bristol, City of, this is in the region of the South West.
